title: Feasibility audit for Taiwan typhoon-holiday volatility mechanism study

verdict.plain_english: The repo has local 0050.TW price history, but it lacks a canonical typhoon-holiday event table and lacks local TAIEX / index-futures price series. That means the requested reopening-gap and holiday-mechanism study cannot yet be executed honestly.

research_question.core: Do typhoon landfalls and typhoon holidays create systematic reopening volatility in Taiwan markets?
proposed_design: Typhoon landfall / warning / market-closure event table
Reopen-day gap and realized-vol study on TAIEX / TXF / 0050.TW

blocking_conditions.detail: No canonical typhoon-holiday event table was found. The study needs exact dates for landfall, warnings, closure decisions, and reopening days.
Local 0050.TW exists, but the broader target design explicitly references TAIEX and TAIFEX. Those local series were not found in reusable canonical form.
The question requires comparison against ordinary long holidays, but there is no canonical Taiwan market-holiday classification table in repo.

typhoon_holiday_event_table.why_needed: Needed to distinguish landfall risk from closure/reopening mechanism.

market_price_cache.why_needed: Needed to separate ETF, cash-index, and futures reopening responses.

holiday_calendar_table.why_needed: Needed for the non-typhoon long-holiday control group.

related_prior_findings.lesson: Taiwan-specific event studies often fail on missing canonical event tables even when local price history exists.
The value of this idea comes from local institutional detail, so using hand-picked dates would defeat the point.

recommended_next_step.phase_1: Build a canonical typhoon-holiday event table from CWB / exchange closure notices.
recommended_next_step.phase_2: Pin local TAIEX / TXF price series alongside 0050.TW.
recommended_next_step.phase_3: Run reopening-gap and realized-vol comparisons vs ordinary long holidays.
